subject.title: [Feature]: Pattern-based channel allowlist for Discord (glob/wildcard support)

question: Should Discord guild channel allowlists support glob-pattern keys such as `ws-*`, and what precedence should those patterns have relative to exact entries, disabled entries, thread-parent fallback, category inheritance, and the literal `*` entry?
rationale: The requested syntax changes a public Discord config surface and determines which guild messages can reach agents, so automation should not choose the authorization semantics on its own.

options.title: Approve narrow glob contract
options.body: Add Discord-owned glob matching with explicit precedence, schema/types/docs, audit/status visibility, and focused ingress tests while keeping category inheritance and access-list redesign separate.

options.title: Fold into access-control redesign
options.body: Keep this open but solve dynamic channel admission through the category or broader Discord access-control trackers before implementing a separate glob syntax.

options.title: Reject glob syntax
options.body: Keep exact entries plus literal `*` and document that dynamic workflows should use wildcard, category inheritance, or another approved access-control design instead.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow glob contract
recommendation.body: Add Discord-owned glob matching with explicit precedence, schema/types/docs, audit/status visibility, and focused ingress tests while keeping category inheritance and access-list redesign separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history on the shared matcher and Discord allowlist precedence surfaces affected by this decision.
